key_insight: A human-supervised LLM guided a change in calibration strategy that improved intensity uniformity in a neutral-atom tweezer array.
engineering_relevance: LLMs may support adaptive quantum-hardware calibration by selecting strategies while deterministic software computes updates and experimentalists authorize waveforms.
method: Use experimental feedback to guide step-by-step LLM strategy selection.
Switch from stalled multiplicative row–column correction to a drift-corrected local response-matrix method.
Delegate image analysis and numerical updates to deterministic software, with human verification of every waveform.
evidence_signal: In a 10×10 crossed-acousto-optic-deflector array, the workflow reduced Gaussian-peak coefficient of variation from 20.30% to 1.57% over 30 candidate-update rounds.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates human-supervised calibration of one hardware subsystem, not autonomous control or improved quantum-computing performance.
paper_title: Large Language Model Steering of Acousto-Optic Tweezer Arrays
